title: Perfluoroalkyl and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFASs) as Indicators for Microleakage Warning and Ecological Risk Identification: A Case Study of a Hazardous Waste Landfill in Northeast China
content:
During landfill microleakage, PFASs can indicate groundwater deterioration more clearly than conventional parameters. Short-chain PFASs can serve as pioneer compounds to delineate the leading edge of the microleakage plume. PFAS assessment reveals potential localized ecological risks in groundwater.


ABSTRACT

Warning of landfill microleakage remains a challenge. However, perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) offer a novel opportunity for sensitive detection. This study investigated a hazardous waste landfill to evaluate the distribution of traditional regulatory parameters and PFASs in surrounding groundwater. Groundwater quality deterioration and ecological risks were assessed using the groundwater contamination index (C d ) and risk quotient (RQ) models. Results identified PFBS and PFBA as pioneer compounds delineating the microleakage plume's leading edge. The PFASs contamination index substantially exceeded that of traditional parameters, contributing over 94% to the overall C d at the leading edge and demonstrating superior sensitivity. Furthermore, trace PFASs concentrations during the microleakage phase can drive localized high ecological risks under the selected NORMAN screening benchmarks. This study confirms that PFASs can warn of water quality deterioration more clearly than traditional parameters during the microleakage phase and highlights the potentially underestimated ecological risks.
